title: [DECISION] Pre-lock validation of ikm_fd and iterations enables early error return
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1738-1768 and 1773-1800: Critical ikm_fd checks (iterations != 0 for HKDF, PBKDF2 with ikm_fd != -1) and the full ikm_fd extraction (fget, lock ks, read key, unlock, fput) happen BEFORE state->lock is acquired at line 1835. This means if ikm_fd is invalid or conflicting with the algorithm, the error is returned immediately without holding any locks. If these checks happened after acquiring state->lock, an error would hold the lock longer than necessary. More importantly, if ikm_fd points to a slow or unresponsive fd (e.g., a socket that blocks), the early validation prevents the calling fd from being blocked on its own lock. The pattern separates pure validation (algorithm-specific checks) from resource acquisition (locking state). This is a non-obvious discipline: less careful code might acquire state->lock first, then do validation inside the lock, increasing lock contention and error latency.
